subject: Metering discrepancy scope + RevRec impact (Feb invoices)
body:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Mei Lin <mei.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 5, 2026 at 8:12 AM PST
Subject: Metering discrepancy scope + RevRec impact (Feb invoices)

Rishi — can you help me get to an answer on scope/materiality today?

We’re seeing a handful of cases where invoice token totals don’t match customer usage exports (Acme is the loudest one, but it’s not only them).

I need:
1) A rough upper bound on exposure (worst-case $) if this is systemic vs isolated.
2) A recommendation on whether we adjust any already-issued invoices or treat as forward-only fixes (with credits where appropriate).
3) What evidence we need to retain for audit (esp. if we decide not to reissue).

Mei attached the current discrepancy sampling sheet + the SQL snippets she used to bucket issues (late events vs retries vs missing dims). Emily has the RevRec impact memo draft.

Attachments:
- invoice-discrepancy-samples-feb-2026.xlsx
- revrec-impact-assessment-meters-vs-contracts.pdf
- meter-sanity-checks-sql-queries-v1.txt

Key link for Acme support thread: jira://customer-support/SUP-28451

If you can send me a quick summary with numbers + recommendation by EOD, I’ll use it in my check-in with Evelyn/Jordan tomorrow.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
CFO, Redwood Inference


----

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Mei Lin <mei.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 5, 2026 at 9:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Metering discrepancy scope + RevRec impact (Feb invoices)

Got it. I’ll quantify in two passes:

A) Sample-based estimate from the 32 invoice-days in the spreadsheet (by account/day/model/region) to get an error distribution (absolute $ and % of invoice).
B) “Mechanism-based” bound using what Mei flagged as likely root causes:
- server-side retries/fallback (potential double-count)
- missing/incorrect region dimension (mis-priced, not necessarily mis-metered)
- late-arriving events vs ledger cutoff

Quick Q: do we have a Finance-approved “materiality threshold” we want to apply here (e.g., <0.5% of monthly usage revenue or <$25k)? Emily’s memo references thresholds but I want to confirm which we’re using for decisioning.

Initial read from a glance at the sample sheet:
- Most deltas look small (<1–2%) and cluster on a couple of models + streaming paths.
- The “big” ones appear to be retry/fallback behavior (which is fixable and could justify credits rather than reissue).

I’ll send a quantified summary by ~2 PM and a final rec by EOD.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
FP&A, Redwood Inference

From: Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mei Lin <mei.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 5, 2026 at 9:41 AM PST
Subject: Re: Metering discrepancy scope + RevRec impact (Feb invoices)

On thresholds: for internal action we’ve generally treated >$50k cumulative or >1% of monthly usage revenue as “requires formal assessment + sign-off.”

From a RevRec perspective (ASC 606):
- If we believe invoices are not in accordance with contract definition of usage, we either correct (reissue) or issue credits depending on timing and practicality.
- For usage-based variable consideration, we can avoid retroactive adjustments if (a) contract language supports our meter definition, (b) issue is immaterial, and (c) we have an audit trail showing why we chose forward-only.

What I’d like to avoid is a pattern of quietly making changes to historical meter logic without documenting the impact.

Mei — can you confirm whether the ledger is currently treating late events as “next day” or is it backfilling into the original usage date? That impacts cutoff and customer expectations.

— Emily
Emily Stone
Accounting / RevRec, Redwood Inference


----

From: Mei Lin <mei.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 5, 2026 at 10:18 AM PST
Subject: Re: Metering discrepancy scope + RevRec impact (Feb invoices)

Confirming current behavior:

- Ledger daily rollups are based on “usage_event_time” with a cutoff window; events arriving after cutoff can land in the next processing run but still attribute to the original usage date IF the event has the original usage timestamp.
- The issue we’ve seen is some late events are missing or have shifted timestamps (ingestion_time used instead of usage_event_time) so they roll into the following day. That’s what causes the usage export (which is often “by day”) to disagree with invoice previews.

For Acme:
- The largest deltas are on streaming requests where the server retries/fallbacks after an upstream timeout.
- We think this is double-counting completion tokens in the usage events (one for the original partial stream, one for the retried stream) even though the customer only sees the final response.

Pointers:
- Slack thread where we pasted the quick query + examples: slack://finance/1770043123-usage-recon-discrepancy-acme
- Tables used:
  - snowflake://REDWOOD_FINANCE.USAGE_RECON.V_USAGE_EVENTS_DAILY
  - snowflake://REDWOOD_FINANCE.BILLING.V_BILLING_LEDGER_DAILY

If useful I can pull a “top 20 accounts by estimated delta $” by 1 PM (would be directional only until we fix the retry classification).

— Mei
Mei Lin
Reconciliation datasets & drift checks

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Mei Lin <mei.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 5, 2026 at 2:07 PM PST
Subject: Re: Metering discrepancy scope + RevRec impact (Feb invoices)

Update (prelim numbers; will refine):

1) Sample-based estimate (from invoice-discrepancy-samples-feb-2026.xlsx)
- Median absolute delta: 0.6% of daily invoice amount
- 75th percentile: 1.4%
- Two outliers: 4.8% and 6.1% (both streaming + retry/fallback signature)

If we project the observed distribution to monthly usage rev, the “expected” exposure is low, but the outlier mechanism is the risk.

2) Mechanism-based upper bound (retry/fallback double-count)
Mei’s query suggests ~0.9% of streaming requests have a retry/fallback in the window. If those are double-counting completions, and if completions are ~55% of tokens on those requests, then worst-case overbilling is roughly:
0.9% * 55% = ~0.5% of total token-billed value on impacted endpoints.

In $ terms, using last month’s Hosted API usage revenue run-rate, that’s < $40k/month in worst-case if systemic across all accounts; likely lower due to model mix.

3) Recommendation
- Do NOT reissue invoices broadly.
- For specific customers with documented deltas (Acme, plus any others >$5k or >3% of invoice), handle via targeted credits once Eng confirms the retry double-count bug and we can quantify.
- Treat meter fix as forward-only with “shadow billing compare” for 1–2 weeks before affecting invoices.

4) Audit trail we should retain
- The pre/post delta calculation from shadow billing (by account/day/model/region)
- A memo (Emily) stating impact assessment + conclusion immaterial except specific exceptions
- A list of credited accounts with approval (CFO + Accounting)

Open item for Laura: confirm whether you want the “customer threshold” for proactive credits to be $5k/3% or something else.

— Rishi


----

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Mei Lin <mei.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 5, 2026 at 4:37 PM PST
Subject: Re: Metering discrepancy scope + RevRec impact (Feb invoices)

This is exactly what I needed.

Decisions:
- Agree: no broad reissues.
- Let’s set proactive credit threshold at: >$5k OR >3% of the invoice for the period in question, AND only when we can tie to a confirmed meter defect (e.g., retry/fallback double-count).
- For anything under that, we’ll respond case-by-case if raised, but we won’t go hunting.

Action items:
1) Rishi: please send me a 1-pager summary I can forward to Evelyn/Jordan (keep it non-technical but with the bound and the recommendation).
2) Emily: finalize the RevRec memo with the threshold, decision, and evidence checklist. Also add language that meter fixes require shadow-billing compare + sign-off.
3) Mei: pull top accounts by estimated delta and tag which ones look like retry/fallback vs late events. For Acme, coordinate with Support on timing/wording (linking SUP-28451).

We need to be very careful that pricing experiment readouts aren’t mixing pre/post meter fix behavior — please flag that as a caveat anywhere this data is used.

Thanks all.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
CFO, Redwood Inference
